foundationscrisis.name: Foundations Crisis: The Limits of Formalization
foundationscrisis.truth: Every formal system has an outside. Complete order is impossible.
foundationscrisis.qfep_connection: Gödel proves pure F-minimization hits a wall. The edge isn't failure—it's constitutive. Systems must oscillate because they cannot close.
foundationscrisis.formula: ∃ statement S: S is true AND S is unprovable
foundationscrisis.description: The 19th-20th century crisis that shattered mathematical certainty. Non-Euclidean geometry, Russell's paradox, Gödel's incompleteness, Brouwer's intuitionism. Each map stages a limit—where formal systems encounter their outside.
learning_objectives: Non-Euclidean geometry: the parallel postulate is independent
Gödel's incompleteness: true statements that cannot be proven
Brouwer's intuitionism: only assert what you can construct
The edge as constitutive, not defective
content: Euclid_Parallel: The fifth postulate—assumed for millennia, independent all along
NonEuclidean_Spaces: Hyperbolic and spherical geometry—alternatives exist
Russell_Paradox: The set of all sets that don't contain themselves
Godel_Incompleteness: This statement is unprovable—self-reference creates the edge
Escher_Impossible: Locally coherent, globally impossible—visual Gödel
Brouwer_Intuitionism: Only assert what you can construct
Florensky_Paraconsistent: A and not-A—holding contradiction without triviality
Crisis_Synthesis: The edge is where the interesting work happens
